properties.name: Sahelanthropus tchadensis
properties.description: One of the oldest known species in the human lineage, known from a cranium ('Toumaï') found in the Djurab Desert of Chad. Possibly near the split between hominins and chimpanzees.

properties.name: Australopithecus afarensis
properties.description: Small-brained, habitually bipedal hominin of East Africa, famous for the 'Lucy' skeleton (Hadar, Ethiopia) and the Laetoli footprints (Tanzania).

properties.name: Homo habilis
properties.description: Early member of the genus Homo from East Africa, long associated with the first stone tools of the Oldowan industry.

properties.name: Homo erectus
properties.description: Long-legged, larger-brained hominin and the first to spread widely beyond Africa, reaching the Caucasus (Dmanisi), China (Zhoukoudian) and Java (Sangiran, Ngandong).

properties.name: Homo neanderthalensis (Neanderthal)
properties.description: Cold-adapted hominins of Europe and western Asia who buried their dead, made sophisticated Levallois/Mousterian tools and interbred with Homo sapiens.

properties.name: Homo sapiens
properties.description: Anatomically modern humans, first known from Jebel Irhoud (Morocco) about 300,000 years ago, later spreading across every continent except Antarctica.

properties.name: Oldowan
properties.description: The oldest widespread stone-tool industry: simple flakes and choppers struck from cobbles, first documented at Gona (Ethiopia) and named after Olduvai Gorge.

properties.name: Acheulean
properties.description: Industry defined by symmetrical bifacial handaxes, made for well over a million years across Africa, western Eurasia and South Asia.

properties.name: Levallois / Mousterian
properties.description: Middle Palaeolithic technology using the Levallois prepared-core technique to produce standardised flakes; strongly associated with Neanderthals but also used by early Homo sapiens.

properties.name: Aurignacian
properties.description: Early Upper Palaeolithic culture of Homo sapiens in Europe, linked to the earliest figurative art (Chauvet Cave, Hohle Fels figurines) and bone flutes.

properties.name: Gravettian
properties.description: Pan-European Upper Palaeolithic culture known for 'Venus' figurines (Willendorf, Dolní Věstonice), mammoth-bone dwellings and elaborate burials.

properties.name: Natufian
properties.description: Late Epipalaeolithic culture of the Levant whose semi-sedentary villages and wild-cereal harvesting set the stage for the invention of agriculture.

properties.name: Linear Pottery (LBK)
properties.description: Early Neolithic farming culture that spread rapidly across central Europe, named for its band-decorated pottery and known for large timber longhouses.

properties.name: Ancient Egypt (Old Kingdom)
properties.description: The 'Age of the Pyramids': a centralised state ruled from Memphis that controlled the Nile valley from the Delta to the First Cataract at Aswan.

properties.name: Ancient Egypt (Middle Kingdom)
properties.description: Reunified Egypt that pushed south into Nubia, fortifying the Second Cataract, and produced a classical age of Egyptian literature.

properties.name: Ancient Egypt (New Kingdom)
properties.description: Egypt at its imperial height under pharaohs such as Thutmose III and Ramesses II, ruling from Nubia's Fourth Cataract to the Levant.

properties.name: Indus Valley Civilisation (Mature Harappan)
properties.description: Bronze Age urban civilisation of planned cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, with standardised weights, drainage systems and a still-undeciphered script.

properties.name: Akkadian Empire
properties.description: Often called the first empire: founded by Sargon of Akkad, it united the Sumerian city-states and Akkadian speakers of Mesopotamia under one ruler.

properties.name: Mycenaean Greece
properties.description: Late Bronze Age Greek palace states such as Mycenae and Pylos, which used Linear B script and later absorbed Minoan Crete.

properties.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
properties.description: Iron Age Mesopotamian superpower ruled from Nimrud and Nineveh, known for its professional army, mass deportations and monumental palace reliefs.

properties.name: Carthage
properties.description: Phoenician colony turned western Mediterranean maritime power, controlling North Africa, Sardinia and western Sicily until its destruction by Rome in 146 BCE. Shown at approximate peak extent.

properties.name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
properties.description: Founded by Cyrus the Great, the largest empire the world had yet seen, stretching from Egypt and Anatolia to the Indus, administered through satrapies and the Royal Road.

properties.name: Roman Empire (Augustan)
properties.description: The Roman state under Augustus after the end of the Republic, encircling the Mediterranean from Hispania and Gaul to Syria and Egypt.

properties.name: Han Dynasty
properties.description: Chinese imperial dynasty that consolidated Qin unification, opened the Silk Road to Central Asia and established Confucianism as state ideology.
